summary: @ornikar/monorepo-config preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers such as _0x488df8 and per-function string-key dispatch tables wrapping fs/https/execFileSync) and, on npm install, checks for a local bun binary or otherwise downloads a Bun v1.3.13 release for the current platform/arch (with musl detection on Linux) from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, unzips to a temp directory, chmods 0755, then invokes execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js]) to run the sibling math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727,680-byte file marked '// @bun @bun-cjs' containing the canonical obfuscator.io string-array shape (large mixed int/string constant table n7gIxM, array-rotation function WV8StW, decoder hc1jfK9 over a scrambled alphabet); its filename 'math_init' is unrelated to the package's declared monorepo-config purpose and its contents are only reachable through the freshly downloaded Bun runtime, bypassing Node-based static analysis. A monorepo configuration package has no legitimate reason to fetch a second language runtime at install time to execute a heavily obfuscated bundled script. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: attacker-controlled behavior executes on the installer's machine at npm install time via a runtime swap that evades Node-only scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
